public_rationale: Anthropic’s April 23 postmortem identifies a Claude Code defect introduced on March 26, 2026. After an idle-session threshold, it repeatedly discarded reasoning history, causing forgetfulness, repetition and odd tool choices [e1]. A firsthand report published April 2 records user-defined stop-hook interventions on multiple days from March 8–25, including 43 on March 18 [e2]. Together, these document recurring practical limitations during March and support the claim under the contract’s qualitative reading of “not perfect or even close” [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence does not establish a representative failure rate across Claude Code users or tasks.
The stop-hook counts measure user-defined workflow interventions, not incorrect code; the report’s proposed cause is not independently established [e2].
Anthropic reports fixing the defect on April 10, 2026; this evidence does not establish that it persisted afterward [e1].

criteria.support_condition: Documented recurring failures or substantial practical limitations in Claude Code during the target month show that users could not rely on consistently correct, unattended operation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, representative evidence establishes consistently near-perfect practical operation across the relevant uses and shows that alleged material failures were erroneous, isolated or outside the target period.
